findings.title: Compilation error: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called with no arguments
findings.body: In `UsernameForm.authenticate`, `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is called without any arguments, but the method defined on the superclass `UsernamePasswordForm` (line 160) has the signature `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. This causes a compilation failure (`method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled in class UsernamePasswordForm cannot be applied to given types`).

findings.title: Passkeys conditional UI is broken for initial login when user is null
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. Because it requires `user != null`, `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is skipped in both `authenticate(context)` (line 115) and `challenge(context, error, field)` (line 137) whenever `context.getUser()` is `null`—which is the normal initial login case before any user has been identified. As a result, the WebAuthn conditional UI form attributes and challenge are never populated on initial login, breaking passkey authentication whenever a user is not already set in the context.
